methods.label: Use the inradius as a common height
methods.explanation:
Joining the incenter to the three vertices divides the triangle into three smaller triangles, each with height equal to the inradius \(r\) when its original side is used as the base. The hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=13\). Equating the whole area to the sum of the smaller areas gives
\[
\frac{5\times12}{2}=\frac{5r}{2}+\frac{12r}{2}+\frac{13r}{2}=15r.
\]
Thus \(30=15r\), and the inradius is \(r=2\).
methods.levelReason: Derives the area-radius relation using elementary triangle areas and the defining equal-distance property of the incenter.
